name: Mexico
headline: Mexico: +0.5% growth in 2025, 3.8% inflation, debt 62% of GDP
sections: Mexico is a $1.84 trillion economy (2025), the world's 16th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $26K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 20.0% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 3.8% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 7.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.6% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 5.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 62% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 59% in 2020. The general government balance is −4.9% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −0.5% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 80% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 65% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 75.3 years (2024). Population: 133.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
